title: Michael Strain: Why the American Economy Keeps Surprising Everyone
summary: AEI economist calls the mid-2026 economy resilient but says underlying inflation is around three percent and tariffs are raising costs for consumers and domestic manufacturers.

assertions.quote: through all of this, the American consumer continues to uh spend and continues to show remarkable resilience

verdicts.note: Retail sales, GDP and the Fed's own assessment showed solid spending growth through 2026 despite the energy shock.

The FOMC's September 16, 2026 statement says domestic spending has been resilient despite elevated geopolitical uncertainty, and BEA lists consumer spending as a contributor to Q2 2026 GDP growth; neither document quantifies spending growth.

assertions.quote: households said, you know, we're going to buy gas, but we're not going to stop buying other stuff. We're just going to save less

verdicts.note: The personal saving rate fell by about two points over the year while real spending held up, which is consistent with dissaving to absorb fuel costs.

assertions.quote: I think underlying inflation is around 3%. I think if anything it's accelerating rather than uh rather than decelerating.

verdicts.note: Core PCE ran near three percent through 2026 and core CPI edged up into the autumn, with no sustained move toward target.

Core CPI ran 2.4-2.9% through 2026 (2.6% in September) and core services 2.9-3.4%, so 'around three' overstates core slightly; and it did decelerate, from 3.0-3.1% in mid-2025 to 2.4% in August 2026, before rebounding to 2.6%.

assertions.quote: underlying inflation was trending back to the Fed's 2% target but was kind of bumped up by tariffs and then bumped up

verdicts.note: Tariff and energy effects are expected to fade, but core measures stayed near three percent through 2026 with services inflation showing no clear downtrend.

On the tariff part only: the tariff contribution to twelve-month goods inflation peaked in February 2026 and is forecast to fade to zero by August 2026, consistent with a temporary lift to inflation; the post says nothing about underlying inflation or the Iran war.

assertions.quote: observes that prices are a lot higher than they were just uh six years ago. And I think the American people are reacting to that

verdicts.note: Consumer sentiment stayed depressed even as inflation slowed in 2023-24, tracking the roughly quarter rise in the price level since 2020.

assertions.quote: We should not want a deflation. We should not want prices to go back to where they were in 2021 or in 2019.

verdicts.note: Broad price declines of twenty percent or more have historically occurred only in severe depressions.

assertions.quote: American businesses and consumers are paying the current tariffs

verdicts.note: Regressions on HTS10-country import data through November 2025 find 94 percent of the tariff incidence fell on U.S. importers in January-August 2025 and 86 percent in November; a 10 percent tariff lowered foreign export prices only 0.6 to 1.4 percent, so U.S. firms and consumers bear the bulk of the burden.

assertions.quote: it was foreignbased companies that would be paying that which almost everyone says is not true

verdicts.note: Foreign exporters bore only 6 to 14 percent of the 2025 tariff incidence by period, with U.S. importers bearing 86 to 94 percent; the staff report's import-price regressions give the same roughly 90 percent border pass-through.

assertions.quote: The president's tariffs are uh contributing meaningfully to measured consumer price inflation.

verdicts.note: The staff report estimates that about 26 percent of a tariff increase passes through to consumer goods prices within a year, 64 percent directly via imported goods and 36 percent via domestically produced goods, and concludes the 2025 tariffs had economically and statistically significant effects on consumer prices.

assertions.quote: the slight majority of what the US imports every year are um uh goods that US businesses need to make stuff here

verdicts.note: The marginal cost channel is the main route into domestic prices: for the average consumer goods industry, which uses 18 percent imported inputs, a 10 percent increase in input duties raises producer prices by 2.6 percent over twelve months, positive and significant in every specification.

assertions.quote: they're registering a lot of a lot of discontent and they're not adding to payrolls

verdicts.note: Business surveys report tariff-related hiring restraint and manufacturing payrolls fell, but overall unemployment stayed near four percent.
